# Detector report (generated by `python -m ml.scripts.train_detector`)

> **These numbers come from SYNTHETIC data.** The household behaviour, the sensor noise and the
> fault signatures are simulated by `ml/scripts/generate_data.py`, and the faults are far more
> regular than real plumbing failures. The metrics below will **not** transfer to real sensors
> without recalibration (per-flat baselines from real data, threshold/operating-point tuning and
> a labelled field validation). See the honesty section at the end.

- Trained: 2026-10-16T16:04:02+00:00 | seed 42 | sklearn 1.9.1
- Data: 12 flats x 30 days (hash `b2493be28dbd215f`), window = 15
  min, stride 5 min
- Split: chronological, train < 2025-01-27T00:00:00+00:00 (72288 windows) /
  test >= split (31104 windows). Baselines (raw per-minute flow per hour-of-week slot)
  use train-period normal data only; IsolationForest (contamination 0.02) fitted on
  62874 train-normal windows.
- Selected hyper-parameters (TimeSeriesSplit(3) on train, macro-F1 0.896):
  `{"max_depth": null, "min_samples_leaf": 1, "n_estimators": 200}`

## Caveats

- Window labels are the fault state at the window end; windows overlap (stride < window), so
  neighbouring test samples are correlated and the effective sample size is small.
- Slow leaks and drips add a constant floor in a world where normal nights are exactly ~0; real
  households (dripping appliances, filling tanks, pressure cycling) are much noisier.
- Timestamps are treated as UTC (= local) in training; the backend converts to its timezone.

## Honesty section (read before quoting any number above)

**Support in episodes, not just windows.** Test period fault episodes (onset after the split):
leak 18, burst 7, overuse 5 (detected at least once:
leak 18, burst 7, overuse 5) across 12 flats.
The window supports in the table count overlapping windows (window 15 min, stride
5 min) of those few episodes - they are NOT independent samples.

**Uncertainty (95% bootstrap CI, 1000 bootstrap resamples over 12 test flats (windows) / 25 leak+burst episodes (episode detection)).**

| metric | point | 95% CI |
|---|---|---|
| macro-F1 | 0.940 | [0.868, 0.962] |
| leak+burst window recall | 0.993 | [0.990, 0.995] |
| leak+burst episode detection (25 episodes) | 1.000 | [1.000, 1.000] |
| overuse precision | 0.709 | [0.245, 0.852] |
| overuse F1 | 0.794 | [0.377, 0.879] |

**Leave-flats-out (4-fold over flats; classifier never sees the held-out flats).**
Pooled macro-F1 0.934 (per fold 0.989, 0.959, 0.901, 0.951), leak+burst recall 0.993, per-class F1 {'normal': 0.997, 'leak': 0.995, 'burst': 0.961, 'overuse': 0.785}. Train windows are from the train period only and held-out flats are scored on the test
period, so this tests unseen households and unseen time together.

**Circularity.** A depth-3 tree on `min_flow` alone gets leak F1 0.994, burst F1
0.826, overuse F1 0.000, macro-F1 0.703 on the same test
set. On this synthetic generator the additive leak/burst floors make `min_flow` highly informative
for leak and burst (F1 above), and the generator's fault ranges (magnitude, L/min or x: slow_leak 0.5-3.0, running_toilet 0.45-0.55, dripping_tap 0.05-0.2, burst 15.0-50.0, overuse 2.0-4.0; duration, min:
slow_leak 360-2160, running_toilet 360-1440, dripping_tap 720-2880, burst 10-120, overuse 60-480) mirror the thresholds of the rule fallback in the backend. High leak/burst scores
therefore show the pipeline is wired correctly, not that real leaks are this separable. Overuse
(multiplicative, overlaps normal peaks) is the hard class and the number to watch.

**Onset to first flag (7 min median, 30/30 episodes).**
Offline classifier, onset to the first window predicted non-normal; ANY non-normal class counts
(a wrong type still counts as detected); quantized by the 5-minute window stride;
excludes alert debounce, MQTT transport and escalation latency; synthetic data only. It is not an
operational time-to-alert.

**Train/serve parity.** Features are computed by `libs/aquaguard_features`, the same code the
backend imports; `ml/tests/test_parity.py` asserts identical vectors and equal classifier F1.
Synthetic timestamps are UTC and treated as local time for the hour-of-week slot and the night
window (local 00:00-05:00); the backend converts to `settings.timezone` first.
